findings.issue_text: Blacklist check in addGuests.handler.ts:77 is case-sensitive against a lowercased list — incoming guest email is compared raw against `blacklistedGuestEmails`, so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
`isTeamAdminOrOwner` at addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses `&&` instead of `||`, so team admins are denied and only owners pass the permission branch

EventManager at addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 is constructed from the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar/video updates run against credentials that don't own the event and silently no-op or fail; `booking.user.credentials` fetched at line 38 is never used
`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in addGuests.schema.ts:4 has no `.max()` bound, allowing unbounded attendee rows and mass emails — an email amplification/spam vector
No booking-state check in addGuests.handler.ts:26-42 — guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings, sending invitation emails and ICS REQUEST files for dead events

`uniqueGuests` at addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 dedupes only against existing attendees, not within the submitted array, so a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails creates duplicate attendee rows (uniqueness refine exists only client-side)
Existing-attendee dedupe at addGuests.handler.ts:76 uses case-sensitive comparison (`guest === attendee.email`), so `A@B.com` is added alongside an existing `a@b.com`

Read of booking.attendees, dedupe, and createMany at addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 are not transactional and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent requests create duplicate attendees and duplicate invitation emails

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at addGuests.handler.ts:168 passes the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`, so filtered-out addresses (existing attendees or blacklisted) receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification

The `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` comparison in packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 is case-sensitive, so new guests submitted with different casing than stored receive the wrong email template

Attendees created at addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 have no corresponding BookingSeat record while the event is copied with seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees, bypassing seat limits and breaking seat-based cancel/reschedule flows
`this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` at packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 is unguarded and throws a TypeError when the attendees array is empty, failing the organizer email

`prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` at addGuests.handler.ts:58-60 throws an unhandled NotFoundError surfaced as a 500 instead of a typed TRPCError for bookings with a null userId (e.g. dynamic-group bookings)
No tests accompany the new handler — the permission matrix, blacklist filter, and dedupe path are all untested
`isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:53-57 is only set to true and cleared on Cancel, so the error banner stays visible after a successful corrected submission
When all email rows are removed, `handleAdd` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51 returns silently with no user feedback — the Add button appears to do nothing

The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44 is dead code because the template string is always non-empty, exposing raw output like `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid` to users
`catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` at addGuests.handler.ts:169-171 discards the error, making email delivery failures undiagnosable in production

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 imports from the `@calcom/ui` barrel that re-exports itself, creating a self-referential cycle and pulling the entire UI barrel into the dynamic chunk, defeating MultiEmailLazy.tsx's lazy-loading purpose

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager at addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 is constructed from the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar/video updates run against credentials that don't own the event and silently no-op or fail; `booking.user.credentials` fetched at line 38 is never used

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `user.credentials` included (the booking organizer’s credentials), but those credentials are never referenced later. Instead, the handler calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the requesting session user (could be an attendee or team admin/owner per the permission checks). The subsequent `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will therefore run using the requester’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which is a correctness issue when the requester does not own/manage the calendar event. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff and the unused fetched `booking.user.credentials` supports the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in addGuests.schema.ts:4 has no `.max()` bound, allowing unbounded attendee rows and mass emails — an email amplification/spam vector

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` permits `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound, and `addGuestsHandler` will (a) `createMany` attendee rows for all filtered `uniqueGuests` and (b) call `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`. Since the permission check allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call this endpoint, an attendee could submit a very large `guests` array to trigger mass DB inserts + outbound emails/calendar updates (spam/amplification/DoS). Nothing in the handler enforces a max length; client-side uniqueness validation does not mitigate server-side abuse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-state check in addGuests.handler.ts:26-42 — guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings, sending invitation emails and ICS REQUEST files for dead events

adjudication.rationale:
The new `addGuestsHandler` loads a booking only by `id` (no additional `where` constraints) and then unconditionally updates attendees, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`.

There is no check against `booking.startTime` / `booking.endTime` (both are used to build the `CalendarEvent`) to prevent adding guests to already-finished bookings, so the handler will still generate and send ICS `REQUEST` emails for events in the past.

Similarly, the handler performs no validation of any booking “state” (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before mutating attendees and sending emails; the diff shows no such guard at all, so if those states exist on `booking` (as the finding suggests), they are not enforced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `uniqueGuests` at addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 dedupes only against existing attendees, not within the submitted array, so a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails creates duplicate attendee rows (uniqueness refine exists only client-side)

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `uniqueGuests` only dedupes against existing attendees and not within the submitted guest list, allowing duplicate emails in the input to result in duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` (especially via direct server calls). adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedupe at addGuests.handler.ts:76 uses case-sensitive comparison (`guest === attendee.email`), so `A@B.com` is added alongside an existing `a@b.com`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, which is a case-sensitive comparison. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., lowercased) before comparison, an existing attendee `a@b.com` would not match an input `A@B.com`, allowing a duplicate attendee differing only by case to be added. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a real correctness issue (also affects the blacklist check, which lowercases blacklist entries but not the incoming `guest`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read of booking.attendees, dedupe, and createMany at addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 are not transactional and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent requests create duplicate attendees and duplicate invitation emails

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a read (findFirst/include attendees) and then a separate write (booking.update with attendees.createMany) without a transaction, so there is a potential race between concurrent requests. However, the proposed finding specifically asserts “there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)”, which is not shown anywhere in this diff, so the duplicate-row outcome is not verifiable from the changes alone (a DB-level unique constraint could prevent duplicates or cause one request to fail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at addGuests.handler.ts:168 passes the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`, so filtered-out addresses (existing attendees or blacklisted) receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters the input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only persists `uniqueGuests` via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input. In sendAddGuestsEmails, the logic checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` while iterating over `calendarEvent.attendees` (which includes existing attendees). If the caller includes an email that is already an attendee, it will be filtered out from `uniqueGuests` (so not actually a new guest), but because it remains in `guests`, that existing attendee will match the `includes` check and incorrectly receive an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification. (Blacklisted emails won’t receive anything because they are not in `calendarEvent.attendees`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` comparison in packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 is case-sensitive, so new guests submitted with different casing than stored receive the wrong email template

Attendees created at addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 have no corresponding BookingSeat record while the event is copied with seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees, bypassing seat limits and breaking seat-based cancel/reschedule flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `addGuests` mutation that appends new rows to `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and then sends emails / updates calendar attendees. Nowhere in the diff is a `BookingSeat` model/table referenced, nor is there any evidence in this change that adding “guests” is supposed to create seat records (as opposed to simply adding attendees on an existing booking). The presence of `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` on the `CalendarEvent` object doesn’t, by itself, prove a required invariant that every attendee must have a `BookingSeat` row or that seat-limits must be re-enforced when adding guests. Therefore the claim about missing `BookingSeat` records and broken seat-based flows is not verifiable from this diff and is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` at packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 is unguarded and throws a TypeError when the attendees array is empty, failing the organizer email

`prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` at addGuests.handler.ts:58-60 throws an unhandled NotFoundError surfaced as a 500 instead of a typed TRPCError for bookings with a null userId (e.g. dynamic-group bookings)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The use of `|| 0` indicates `booking.userId` may be null/undefined. If it is null (e.g., a booking without an associated user), the query becomes `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw Prisma’s not-found exception, which is not converted to a `TRPCError` in this handler. That would surface as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR/500 rather than a typed TRPC error, making the finding a real correctness issue introduced/contained in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests accompany the new handler — the permission matrix, blacklist filter, and dedupe path are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `addGuests` TRPC mutation/handler with permission checks, blacklist filtering, and guest deduping logic, but it does not add any test files or test coverage alongside it. However, the proposed finding is about missing tests rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code itself. From the diff alone, we can confirm no tests were added, but lack of tests is a quality/process concern, not an intrinsic functional problem in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:53-57 is only set to true and cleared on Cancel, so the error banner stays visible after a successful corrected submission

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails (`handleAdd`), but it is never reset to `false` on a subsequent valid submission path (when `safeParse` succeeds) nor in the mutation `onSuccess`. The only reset is in the Cancel button handler. Therefore, after the user corrects the emails and clicks Add, the error banner can remain visible while the request is pending, and if the dialog is closed/reopened after success, the banner will still be visible because `isInvalidEmail` stayed `true`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When all email rows are removed, `handleAdd` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51 returns silently with no user feedback — the Add button appears to do nothing

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, users can delete email rows via MultiEmail's remove handler (onClickAddon splices the array). If they remove the last row, multiEmailValue becomes an empty array. handleAdd() explicitly checks `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` and does not show any toast or set an error state, so clicking the “Add” button results in no visible action/feedback. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a real UX defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44 is dead code because the template string is always non-empty, exposing raw output like `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid` to users

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)`. A template literal always returns a string, so `message` will be truthy even if `err.data?.code` is undefined (e.g. "undefined: ...") or the translation key is missing, meaning the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback will never be used. This is directly verifiable from the diff. The user-visible text can therefore include raw/error-code-ish prefixes (e.g. "BAD_REQUEST: ...") rather than the intended generic fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` at addGuests.handler.ts:169-171 discards the error, making email delivery failures undiagnosable in production

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try/catch`, but the catch block only logs a static message (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`) and does not include the actual error (`err`), report it to a logger/monitoring system, or propagate it. This makes failures to send emails difficult to diagnose in production and silently masks delivery problems. This behavior is directly present in the diff at the referenced lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 imports from the `@calcom/ui` barrel that re-exports itself, creating a self-referential cycle and pulling the entire UI barrel into the dynamic chunk, defeating MultiEmailLazy.tsx's lazy-loading purpose

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component (which lives inside the `@calcom/ui` package) imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui` (the package barrel). The diff also changes the barrel (`packages/ui/index.tsx`) to export `MultiEmail` via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`. This creates a verifiable circular dependency: `MultiEmail.tsx -> @calcom/ui (index.tsx) -> MultiEmailLazy -> dynamic(import('./MultiEmail')) -> MultiEmail.tsx`. Additionally, importing from the barrel within the lazily-loaded module will tend to pull the barrel (and its transitive exports) into the dynamic chunk, undermining the intent of `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` (“not every user needs” / keep it small).
